briefings.title: Eclipse's Lior Susan on $12.5B AUM and the Bet on Physical Industries
briefings.tldr: Eclipse has reached ~$12.5B in AUM and closed $1.3B in April 2026 for Fund VI and Early Growth III, driven by a thesis that physical industries comprise 85% of global GDP ($100 trillion) and require hands-on operators rather than passive capital.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Eclipse has reached ~$12.5B in AUM and closed $1.3B in April 2026 for Fund VI and Early Growth III, driven by a thesis that physical industries comprise 85% of global GDP ($100 trillion) and require hands-on operators rather than passive capital. Founder & CEO Lior Susan leads the firm alongside 96-year-old co-founder Pierre Lamond, utilizing an intensive incubation model that has built 30 of its 90 total portfolio companies.

## Firm Origins & The "Operators with Capital" Model
* **Background & Founding:** 
  * Founded in 2015 by Lior Susan (who left Flex) and Pierre Lamond (who started at Fairchild, co-founded National Semiconductor, and spent 35+ years at Sequoia Capital).
  * Lior Susan recounts meeting Lamond in early 2015 when Susan was 31 and Lamond was 85; Lamond told him "we're going to start a firm together" four months later.
  * Lamond still mentors the team and recently celebrated his 96th birthday.
* **Operating Philosophy:** 
  * Positioned as "operators with capital" rather than traditional venture capitalists.
  * Emphasizes discipline, institutional knowledge, and hands-on crisis management—such as Susan spending 72 hours in the Midwest handling a severe water-cooling leakage in a portfolio data center.

## Fund Performance & Milestone Investments
* **AUM and Fundraising:** 
  * Manages approximately $12.5B in AUM.
  * Closed $1.3B in April 2026 across Eclipse Fund VI and Early Growth III (the firm's largest raise to date).
  * Portfolio companies have raised $15.9B in 2026 alone.
* **Major Portfolio Outcomes:** 
  * **Cerebras:** 2016 Series A investment; returned roughly $2.5B at the $185 IPO price in May 2026 on about $147M total invested.
  * **SpaceX:** Named alongside Cerebras as recent successful IPOs in physical industries.
  * **Other Noteworthy Portfolio Companies:** Bright Machines, Bedrock, Maitra, Mind, Ursa Major, Vulcan forms, Auggury, Skyrise, Oxide, Wave, True Anomaly, Redwood Materials, Arc (The Nuclear Company), Verata, Anduril, and Peak Energy.

## Incubation Strategy & The "Eclipse Economy"
* **Incubation Model:** 
  * 30 out of Eclipse's 90 total portfolio companies were built/incubated internally.
  * Keeps the team's operating skills fresh by actively carving out and recruiting teams (e.g., spinning out **Mind** from Rivian with RJ Scaringe after three years of discussions).
* **The "Eclipse Economy" (Full-Stack Infrastructure):** 
  * Integrates investments across the entire physical AI and compute stack: chips (Cerebras), manufacturing racks and hardware, server infrastructure (Oxide), nuclear/sodium-ion/gas turbine energy sources, and physical robotics (Maitra, Mind).
  * Leverages internal portfolio cross-collaboration on multi-billion dollar commercial deals.

## Macro Thesis: Physical vs. Software
* **The $100 Trillion Opportunity:** 
  * 85% of world GDP (~$100 trillion) resides in the physical world. 
  * Metal manufacturing alone is a $3 trillion industry that historically received near-zero venture dollars compared to crowded enterprise software markets.
* **Re-evaluating Software Metrics:** 
  * Traditional Silicon Valley obsession with 85% SaaS gross margins often masks cash burn hidden in R&D accounting tricks.
  * Free cash flow and solving massive, difficult physical markets (like energy, manufacturing, and defense) dictate true long-term value, comparing favorably to modern giants like Tesla.

## Notable Quotes
> *"We never thought ourselves as venture capital. We call it operators with capital because we are operators with capital."* — Lior Susan

> *"You cannot fake it till you make it when you're manufacturing something because the yield will just be very bad."* — Lior Susan

> *"What you cannot fight against is 85% of the world GDP, roughly 100 trillion, is in the physical world."* — Lior Susan

briefings.title: Naveen Rao: 4D Computing, AI's Energy Wall & Beating Biology
briefings.tldr: Unconventional AI has developed the world's first physical dynamical computer—a 4D computing chip that merges memory and compute without von Neumann architecture—achieving a thousandfold improvement in energy efficiency to solve AI's impending power wall.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Unconventional AI has developed the world's first physical dynamical computer—a 4D computing chip that merges memory and compute without von Neumann architecture—achieving a thousandfold improvement in energy efficiency to solve AI's impending power wall.

## The Energy Crisis in AI
* **Exponential Token Growth:** **Google** alone crosses 3.2 quadrillion tokens per month, demanding roughly 12 gigawatts of power for AI services alone (with total U.S. data center capacity sitting around 40 gigawatts).
* **The Power Wall Timeline:** **Naveen Rao** estimates the industry will run out of energy within roughly 3 years due to the massive gap between exponential AI market demand and linearized energy supply.
* **Cost Structure Shift:** Energy now accounts for roughly 50% of the cost of serving a token, forcing data center operators to prioritize securing power contracts above all else.

## The Biological Paradigm & 4D Computing Architecture
* **Biological Efficiency:** Human and animal brains operate on remarkably low energy—ranging from a 20-watt human cortex down to an 8-milliwatt squirrel brain capable of highly precise, complex navigation.
* **Eliminating Data Movement:** Standard GPU computing systems move nearly 30 trillion bits in and out of memory per second outside the chip (and 10x-100x more inside), whereas the human cortex moves only about 16 billion bits per second.
* **The 4D Dynamical Computer:** **Unconventional AI** built a chip using "4D computing," leveraging three physical spatial dimensions (including die stacking) and one time dimension in the dynamics. 
* **Integrated Memory and Compute:** Unlike traditional von Neumann architectures that shuttle data back and forth between separate memory and processors, dynamical computers combine compute and memory into a single element where individual computing elements act as memory.

## Technological Breakthroughs & Prototyping
* **Dynamical Systems & Sparsity:** By utilizing dynamical systems theory (emergent behaviors from simple interconnected components, akin to synchronizing metronomes) and introducing *sparsity* (discarding non-essential connections), the system becomes more scalable, trainable, and performant.
* **Rapid Hardware Prototyping:** Starting in January, the team taped out their first physical dynamical computer design to the fab on June 1st (5 months later) and successfully generated the world's first images from such a computer.
* **Power Efficiency Gains:** The physical prototype achieves image generation at roughly 500 nanojoules per image, representing orders of magnitude greater efficiency than standard GPUs.

## Product Roadmap, Software, and Team Dynamics
* **Product Form Factor:** **Naveen Rao** states the company is building a full data center rack system (a new data center product) where users feed tokens in and get tokens out through a network cable, while the inner guts run on dynamical computing.
* **Model Compatibility:** Existing AI models are ported at the model layer rather than the operations layer; the system implements time-varying behaviors that can be characterized mathematically as state transitions without relying on traditional linear algebra/floating-point hardware math.
* **Multidisciplinary Workforce:** **Naveen Rao** notes the company bridges a massive talent gap by combining theorists with math/theoretical neuroscience PhDs (studying dynamical systems) with physical chip architects, coordinated through a Python-based software library designed to express stochastic, time-varying elements.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Naveen Rao** predicts the industry will run out of energy within roughly 3 years.
* **Naveen Rao** sets a timeline of within 2 years to deliver a full data center rack product to market.
* **Naveen Rao** targets hitting the physical limits of 2D lithography within 3 and a half years (accelerated from an initial 5-year estimate).
* **Naveen Rao** states the overarching long-term goal of Unconventional AI is to beat biology in intelligence-per-watt efficiency within the next decade or so.

## Notable Quotes
> "I don't think you really understand something until you can build it."
> — **Naveen Rao**

> "Computers have been built up with these abstractions... each one of these abstractions actually is lossy. It means it's inefficient. It doesn't contemplate all the complexity underneath it."
> — **Naveen Rao**

> "We want to beat biology. We want to make something better and enable compute everywhere including compute in new robotic forms... in the next decade or so."
> — **Naveen Rao**

briefings.title: QIA, Apollo & Goldman CEOs on Global Capital
briefings.tldr: Global capital allocators emphasize that deploying capital successfully requires looking past daily noise to focus on 5-to-20-year trends, navigating an unprecedented technology supercycle, and managing structural shifts across energy, infrastructure, and geopolitical fragmentation.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Global capital allocators emphasize that deploying capital successfully requires looking past daily noise to focus on 5-to-20-year trends, navigating an unprecedented technology supercycle, and managing structural shifts across energy, infrastructure, and geopolitical fragmentation.

## Macro Trends & Geopolitical Fragmentation

*   **Long-Term Forces:** **Mohammed Saif Al-Sowaidi** identifies four structural forces driving multi-generational funds: AI innovation, geopolitics and trade, demographic shifts, and fiscal discipline/non-physical balance sheets.
*   **Capital Abundance vs. Ideas:** **David M. Solomon** notes that capital is a commodity while governance, security, innovation, and open markets are scarce and drive capital to productive locales.
*   **Geopolitical Friction & Supply Chains:** **David M. Solomon** observes that the current period of fragmentation and trade barriers will persist, requiring a long-term view rather than short-term reactivity. **Mohammed Saif Al-Sowaidi** adds that fragmentation pushes up inflation and increases the CapEx required for defense and infrastructure.
*   **Supply Chain Resilience:** **Marc Rowan** argues that current de-risking and supply chain testing are positive, noting that not addressing these risks for 15 years was more dangerous than addressing them now.

## The AI Supercycle & Infrastructure Demands

*   **CapEx and Financing Scale:** **Mohammed Saif Al-Sowaidi** points out that AI capital expenditure is the largest ever privately financed infrastructure spend, with hyperscaler and related spending projected to reach $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion over the next five years.
*   **Energy Constraints:** **Marc Rowan** notes that energy accounts for 50% to 60% of what people expect to enable AI, shifting constraints from silicon to gigawatts and megawatts. **Mohammed Saif Al-Sowaidi** adds that the U.S. has not built energy capacity in 25 years but is now moving quickly into natural gas, nuclear, and other options.
*   **Market Concentration & Risk:** **Marc Rowan** highlights that 10 companies now comprise 50% of the S&P 500 and are all leveraged to the exact same AI trend, leaving markets vulnerable to return-on-investment realities despite fundamental change.
*   **The Application Layer:** **David M. Solomon** states that the real value over the next 10 to 20 years will be created at the application layer and through the S&P "490" companies deploying AI to improve operating efficiency and earnings growth.

## Investment Strategies & Asset Allocation

*   **Diversified Portfolio Construction:** **Mohammed Saif Al-Sowaidi** outlines a balanced portfolio approach: allocating roughly 60% to innovation and the remaining portion to free cash flow-generating businesses, private credit, or infrastructure isolated from disruption.
*   **Private Markets & Dry Powder:** **Mohammed Saif Al-Sowaidi** notes that private equity has grown to $3.5 trillion to $4 trillion, but distributions back to investors remain low relative to massive infrastructure and energy capital requirements.
*   **Physical Defense & Manufacturing:** **Marc Rowan** identifies physical AI, robotics, and defense technology as high-growth areas where 10-to-15-year replacement cycles will compress significantly.
*   **Regional Allocation & Europe:** **Marc Rowan** notes that Europe is currently lagging due to a less flexible financial system and lower historical hospitality to capital, though change is underway. **Mohammed Saif Al-Sowaidi** highlights Southeast Asia as a promising region.

## Fiscal Policy, Debt & Inflation

*   **US Debt and Growth:** **David M. Solomon** and **Marc Rowan** both express comfort with 5% 10-year Treasury yields, noting that rates at or above 5% characterized much of their professional lives without crushing productivity. However, **David M. Solomon** cautions that unchecked fiscal expansion and debt will become economic headwinds if continuous compounded economic growth does not outpace them.
*   **Inflation Outlook:** **Mohammed Saif Al-Sowaidi** flags inflation as a major factor to watch over the next 12 to 24 months, warning of potential stagflation risks and weakened consumer investment capacity due to persistent energy costs.

## Notable Quotes

> "Capital drives what we all do. And at the end of the day, capital looks for opportunity... What's not a commodity is ideas. Locales. Security. Innovation. Open markets."
> — David M. Solomon

> "In short, we're spending every dollar euro pound since the invention of fire. The demand for capital is overwhelming, and I think capital will go wherever it is respected."
> — Marc Rowan

> "While there is that opportunities, there are also risks, involved... You need to be extremely selective because such a large cycle and a long cycle. It will take a lot of time to adapt."
> — Mohammed Saif Al-Sowaidi

briefings.title: Secretary Bessent on CNBC’s Squawk Box

people.name: Scott Bessent
people.role: Secretary of the Treasury, U.S. Department of the Treasury

briefings.tldr: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent detailed ongoing US-China economic and AI diplomatic talks, outlined aggressive new sanction implementations against Iran, and discussed macroeconomic conditions including bond market stability and inflation management.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent detailed ongoing US-China economic and AI diplomatic talks, outlined aggressive new sanction implementations against Iran, and discussed macroeconomic conditions including bond market stability and inflation management.

## US-China Relations and Trade Talks
- **Leadership Rapport as Foundation:** Discussions stem from the strong personal relationship between President Trump and Xi Jinping.
  - Xi Jinping is scheduled to visit Washington this week, following a potential additional two meetings between the leaders to ensure relationship stability.
- **Trade Deal Operationalization:** U.S. Trade Representative Jameson Greer operationalized the "30 by 30 trade deal" for non-critical goods, stemming from discussions in Beijing.
  - **U.S. Export Goals:** Bring non-critical items down to most-favored-nation tariff levels to sell more agriculture, energy, and medical devices.
  - **Chinese Import Goals:** Bring in more everyday consumer items.

## Artificial Intelligence Dialogues and Safety
- **Formalized Framework:** Established the "USA-China AI Dialogues" following 12 hours of working-level talks in Beijing.
  - **Communications and Safety:** Opening an incident communications line and discussing protocols for leading AI dangers (uncontrollable agents, non-state actors in cyber and bioweapons).
- **Global Leadership Status:** Bessent noted that Chinese counterparts acknowledged the U.S. remains the clear leader in powerful AI models.
- **Liability and Frontier Labs:** 
  - Bessent agreed with MIT AI Lab lead Daniel Huttenlocher that humans—specifically lab management (e.g., OpenAI, Hugging Face)—are responsible for AI actions, not agents or the models themselves.
  - Criticized frontier AI labs for pushing a narrative of potential extinction-level events (cited as a 10% chance) while simultaneously seeking government liability shields.
  - Highlighted massive historical valuations for companies like Anthropic, noting they started as small groups in San Francisco during COVID (2021) with valuations soaring from $1 trillion to $2 trillion over five years.
- **Defense and Resiliency:** Emphasized the need for systemic defense, noting that systemically important banks handle millions of attacks daily with elite cybersecurity, serving as a model for smaller banks through the "Gold Eagle" AI workshop/forum.

## Iran Sanctions and Enforcement
- **Expanded Authorities:** Treasury has implemented five new sanctions authorities granted about a month ago targeting the Iranian regime across aviation, maritime, crypto, and gold.
- **Enabler Crackdown:** 
  - Targeted international financial enablers funneling funds to the regime, specifically shutting down external branches of the second-largest bank in Egypt (funneled >$1.8 billion), the ~30th largest Turkish bank, and the second-largest Russian bank.
  - Enacting measures against Iranian airlines, stating all Iranian airlines will be shut down globally, prohibiting fuel, landing services, and ticket sales under threat of exclusion from the dollar system.

## Macroeconomic Environment and Markets
- **Interest Rates and Oil Correlation:** Observed an exceptionally high R-squared correlation between 10-to-30-year bond yields, crude oil prices, and the crack spread since the conflict started.
  - Bessent predicts that once past the current conflict, oil markets will be oversupplied and interest rates should decline.
- **Treasury Market Operations:** Defended the decision to increase long-end Treasury buyback size during a highly illiquid period when markets were moving quickly away from equilibrium.
  - Noted that following the increased buyback size announcement, despite surging oil prices and global rate increases, the 30-year Treasury yield rose by only 1 basis point.
- **Federal Reserve Confidence:** Expressed full confidence in Chair Kevin Warsh (who recently raised rates by a quarter point), noting the President also has high confidence that Warsh will balance the inflation and growth mandates.
  - Core inflation remains very quiescent, with current price pressures isolated to headline inflation driven by energy supply shocks.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Treasury Secretary Bessent:** The USA-China AI Dialogues will meet again in approximately two months in Shenzhen.
- **Treasury Secretary Bessent:** On September 23rd, all Iranian airlines will be shut down globally, stopping them from receiving fuel, landing services, or selling tickets worldwide.

## Notable Quotes
> "These labs came out or one lab in specific, a sitting employee came out, said there's a 10% chance of an extinction level event, but then the labs also said, 'Take the liability off of our hands.' And we will not do that." - Scott Bessent on AI lab liability demands
> 
> "On September 23rd, all of the Iranian airlines will be shut down around the world... if they land, you cannot provide them with fuel, you cannot provide them with landing services, you cannot sell them tickets or you will be knocked out of the dollar system." - Scott Bessent on enforcement actions against Iran

briefings.title: Stock Picking in Difficult Times with George Noble | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 76
briefings.tldr: George Noble and Steve Eisman break down current macroeconomic pressures, including Scott Bessent's failed attempts to repress interest rates, the structural risks of the AI capex boom, the unwinding yen carry trade, and massive overvaluations in speculative momentum darlings like Tesla and SpaceX.
briefings.summary_markdown:
### TL;DR
George Noble and Steve Eisman break down current macroeconomic pressures, including Scott Bessent's failed attempts to repress interest rates, the structural risks of the AI capex boom, the unwinding yen carry trade, and massive overvaluations in speculative momentum darlings like Tesla and SpaceX.

---

### Macro & Interest Rates: Scott Bessent's Policy Battles
* **The Fiscal & AI Pressures:** 
  * Total US federal debt has reached **$40 trillion**.
  * Upward pressure on interest rates is primarily driven by the capital expenditure explosion of AI infrastructure rather than standard deficit spending alone.
  * Without the AI demand story, 10-year Treasury yields would likely be **40 basis points lower**.
* **Treasury Secretary Intervention:** 
  * Scott Bessent's attempts to repress interest rates are likened to "bringing a water gun to a real battle" or trying to "kill a whale with a BB gun."
  * Bessent faces a severe credibility threat if rates breach 5% in the near term, given his public interventions.
* **The Japan Currency & Swap Deal:** 
  * Japan intervened with **$95 billion** in a single week to defend the collapsing yen.
  * Rather than selling US Treasuries and driving up domestic yields, Japan bypassed open market selling by securing a Federal Reserve swap line loan to buy domestic Japanese Government Bonds (JGBs).
  * Japan's 10-year JGB yield recently crossed **4%** for the first time in 30 years, though fair value relative to its **240% debt-to-GDP ratio** should be closer to **7%** (compared to the US debt-to-GDP of **125-130%** and a 10-year yield of **4.8%**).

### The AI Ecosystem & Capital Expenditure
* **The Bear Case & The ROI Question:** 
  * The entire AI infrastructure buildout is described as a hybrid of the dot-com bubble and subprime housing collapse, entirely dependent on circular financing and "funny money."
  * **Macro Strategy UK analysis:** Malinvestment in AI is calculated at **24 times** the level seen during the dot-com era.
* **Ecosystem Concentration Risk:** 
  * Approximately **70% of AI revenue** for hyperscalers comes from just two entities: OpenAI and Anthropic.
  * OpenAI and Anthropic represent **25% to 35%** of the hyperscalers' entire cloud revenue.
  * **Nvidia AR Concentration:** In Nvidia's recent quarter, **70% of accounts receivable** came from just **five accounts**.
* **Global Cost-Cutting Pressures:** 
  * Chinese competitors are releasing models that are **95% cheaper** with comparable utility for **95% of users**, undercutting high-cost US LLMs.

### The Changing Investing Environment: Narrative Dominance
* **The Rise of Narrative Over Fundamentals:** 
  * Traditional equity research (6-8 page reports covering balance sheets, cash flows, and SWOT analyses) has been replaced by **"narrative dominance"**—investors prioritizing stories and passive index momentum over P/E ratios and financial validation.
* **Passive Inflows:** 
  * Global liquidity and foreign capital influxes (such as Japanese and European pension fund allocations) have propped up US tech valuations despite a lack of traditional price discovery.

### Tesla & SpaceX: Overvaluation and Structural Shorts
* **SpaceX Fundamentals:** 
  * Market capitalization sits at **$1.7 trillion**, heavily driven by narrative rather than fundamentals.
  * Starlink is estimated to be worth **$200 billion to $300 billion**, while the AI/Grok component is considered a third-tier asset.
  * **Float Expansion Risk:** Insider lockups are expiring, and the public float is expanding from **5%** toward **25%**, introducing significant institutional selling pressure.
  * Sum-of-the-parts valuation points to a share value closer to **$140** versus current market pricing.
* **Tesla Fundamentals:** 
  * US auto sales dropped **26%** in July, with concurrent declines in Europe and China.
  * Capital expenditures are surging to **$30 billion** this year (up from depreciation running at **$6 to $8 billion**), pushing the company deeply cash-flow negative.
  * **Robotaxi Skepticism:** Austin ride-to-population utilization data indicates the robo-taxi total addressable market is heavily overcooked.
  * Sum-of-the-parts valuation implies a fair value of **$30 to $60 per share**.

---

### Predictions & Forward Calls
* **George Noble:** Predicts that the current passive momentum in mega-cap technology, Tesla, and SpaceX will break as liquidity tightens, ultimately pulling valuations down to fundamental realities.
* **George Noble:** Claims that SpaceX and Tesla are both "outstanding shorts" with implied fair values drastically lower than their current multi-trillion-dollar valuations.

---

### Notable Quotes
> *"Sometimes years go by and nothing happens and sometimes weeks go by and years happen."* — **George Noble**

> *"The market constantly overestimated inflation pre-COVID, and since 2022, the market's been constantly underestimating inflation because we have fiscal dominance."* — **George Noble**

> *"When I started in this business, I thought people want to be told the truth. No, they don't want to be told the truth. They want to be told a story that'll make them feel good."* — **Guy Dami (cited by George Noble)**

> *"Forget about the sender financing, the valuation... I'm weighing in with narrative dominance. Don't tell me about the fundamentals and the PE and the valuation... Tell me a story."* — **George Noble**
